lines.trans: Here we are at the municipal clock tower—and the shadow points straight to this park!
Let me read Card Three: Find the iron bench where the oldest linden tree drops its leaves.
That is easy; the oldest linden tree is right there in the centre.
And there is a green iron bench sitting perfectly in its shade!
Come on, let us see if there is another carved symbol waiting for us.
Wait—look at the wooden slats on the back of the bench!
There is a tiny star carved into the wood! We found the third clue!
Excellent! Card Three says: Open the small envelope when all four corners meet.
We only have three cards! Where is Card Four?
Did we drop it in the alley? No, wait—look at the back of Card Three!
It says: Card Four is always where you started.
We started at Jasmine Courtyard! Do we have to walk all the way back?!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أبراج.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: The word 'أشر' (b-ta'asher) means 'she points'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هون بالزبط تحت المصب! ورقة حجر بتأشر للشمال الغربي طالعة التلة الخفيفة!
examples.trans: Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
This is أشر.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word (from Turkish doğru) meaning 'straight ahead' in directions.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: The word 'حديقة' (la-hal-Hadeeqa) means 'to this park'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هينا وصلنا لبرج الساعة البلدي—والخيال بيأشر دغري لهالحديقة!
examples.trans: Here we are at the municipal clock tower—and the shadow points straight to this park!
This is حديقة.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: The word 'لاقى' (nlaaqeeh) means 'we find it'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق شوفوا منيح عالكرت الأول عشان نشوف شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه.
examples.trans: Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
This is لاقى.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: The word 'أقدم' (aqdam) means 'oldest'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أقرأ الكرت التالت: لاقوا المقعد الحديد وين أقدم شجرة زيزفون بتوقع ورقها.
examples.trans: Let me read Card Three: Find the iron bench where the oldest linden tree drops its leaves.
This is أقدم.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: The word 'زيزفون' (zeezafoon) means 'linden'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أقرأ الكرت التالت: لاقوا المقعد الحديد وين أقدم شجرة زيزفون بتوقع ورقها.
examples.trans: Let me read Card Three: Find the iron bench where the oldest linden tree drops its leaves.
This is زيزفون.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: The word 'هادا' (haada) means 'this'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بسيطة! هادا نافورة الحجر المنحوتة الصغيرة بآخر الشارع تبعنا!
examples.trans: Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
This is هادا.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موجودة, plural: موجودين).

examples.trans: Your glasses are right there on your forehead!
Tariq is down in the workshop.

meanings.note: The word 'هنيك' (hneek) means 'there'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا سهل؛ أقدم شجرة زيزفون موجودة هنيك بالنص.
examples.trans: That is easy; the oldest linden tree is right there in the centre.
This is هنيك.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاعدة, plural: قاعدين).

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: The word 'ظل' (b-Zillha) means 'in its shade'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وفي مقعد حديد أخضر قاعد بالزبط بظلها!
examples.trans: And there is a green iron bench sitting perfectly in its shade!
This is ظل.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian/Levantine encourager ('come on! / let us...!').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: The word 'رمز' (el-ramz) means 'the symbol'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق شوفوا منيح عالكرت الأول عشان نشوف شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه.
examples.trans: Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
This is رمز.

meanings.note: The word 'منحوت' (el-manHoote) means 'carved'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بسيطة! هادا نافورة الحجر المنحوتة الصغيرة بآخر الشارع تبعنا!
examples.trans: Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
This is منحوت.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نجوم.

examples.trans: The sky is clear and full of stars tonight.
The guesthouse service deserves five stars!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: The word 'لقي' (laqeena) means 'we found'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: في نجمة صغيرة منحوتة بالخشب! لقينا الدليل التالت!
examples.trans: There is a tiny star carved into the wood! We found the third clue!
This is لقي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أدلة.

examples.trans: I bought the Amman travel guide.
The guesthouse is listed in the annual guide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ممتازة, plural: ممتازين).

examples.trans: The reading light beside the desk is excellent.
The shower water was hot and excellent!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'التقى' (telteqi) means 'she meets'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ممتاز! الكرت التالت بقول: افتحوا المغلف الصغير لما الزوايا الأربعة تلتقي.
examples.trans: Excellent! Card Three says: Open the small envelope when all four corners meet.
This is التقى.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: The word 'تلات' (tlaat) means 'three'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is تلات.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكتوبة, plural: مكتوبين).

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'بدي' (badeena) means 'we started'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إذن الاختصار المشهور تبع الدقيقتين رجعنا دغري لبوابتنا اللي بدينا منها.
examples.trans: So the famous two-minute shortcut brings us straight back to our own starting gate.
This is بدي.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The word 'احنا' (iHna) means 'we'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أها! شوفوا هالحيط التاريخي الهادي—أكيد احنا بالزبط ورا ساحة الساعة!
examples.trans: Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
This is احنا.

meanings.note: The word 'بـ' (b-) means 'in'. It is a common prep in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: احنا بدينا بـ بيت الياسمين! لازم نمشي كل هالطريق نرجع؟!
examples.trans: We started at Jasmine Courtyard! Do we have to walk all the way back?!
This is بـ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The word 'الياسمين' (الياسمين) means 'الياسمين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is الياسمين.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
